messages:
maria: Heads-up — Customer ACME just opened a ticket, high tail latency and unexpected hosted billing despite having a dedicated EU pool pin.
aj: Can you paste the customer id and an example request id? I can look at routing logs.
maria: customer_id=acme-inc, request_id=req_0a9f3b, reported 503s && a lot of 300-700ms p95s. They say most traffic should hit dedicated-eu-1.
sasha: Looking at audit — their pin ttl was refreshed yesterday but I see a few requests routed to hosted-eu-2 around 11:12UTC. Might be overflow/backfill.
leo: @aj quick check: was there any scheduled eviction or node drain in dedicated-eu-1? infra-bot should have posted.
infra-bot: deploy-scheduler: drain started on pool dedicated-eu-1 at 11:10:14 UTC for kernel patch. Expected capacity reduction: 20%. :wrench:
aj: That would explain spillover. But why auth failures/503? Spillover should route to healthy hosted with same model. Are they getting auth errors or rate-limit?
maria: Ticket excerpt: "We saw 401s for a subset of requests after the fallback, then increased latency and a sudden spike in hosted billing charges. Not clear why some requests 401 and others 200."
sasha: 401s could be because token-scoping differs between dedicated and hosted pools (we have a known issue when route changes drop per-namespace auth headers). Can you share raw request headers? maria?
maria: Pasted minimal log: ```
RequestID: req_0a9f3b
x-cust-id: acme-inc
x-route-pin: dedicated-eu-1
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX (scoped:d:c:eu)
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
```
leo: And routing decision log: ```
[11:12:18 UTC] req_0a9f3b -> pool: hosted-eu-2 (spillover), reason=capacity_shortage
[11:12:19 UTC] auth_check -> token_scope mismatch: token_scope=d:c:eu allowed_pools=[dedicated-eu-1,dedicated-eu-2]
[11:12:19 UTC] result -> DENY -> returned 401 to client
```
aj: That matches: token scoped only for dedicated pools, hosted pools reject. We should have automatic token re-scope/forwarding but that isn't implemented. This is an auth-policy gap.
sasha: Action items: (1) Short-term: add a targeted rollback of the drain or move ACME entirely to dedicated-eu-2 as an emergency fix. (2) Medium-term: ensure fallback routing preserves token scoping or reauths with gateway creds and proxies identity.
maria: Customer is asking for repro steps; they want to validate in their staging. Here's a simple repro we used:
1) Create pin to dedicated-eu-1 with ttl 24h. 2) Simulate capacity reduction on dedicated-eu-1 via our admin CLI: `infractl drain-pool --pool dedicated-eu-1 --pct 25` 3) Send 100 concurrent requests with token scoped to dedicated pools. 4) Observe some 401s and overflow to hosted-eu-2. 
leo: For billing spike: hosted requests count against hosted usage even if user has dedicated commit. Their billing attribution rule uses pool tag; spillover -> hosted pricing. Need to notify billing Ops to waive charges for affected window.
aj: I can generate a signed proof log for billing: show timestamps, request ids routed to hosted, and customer pin active. Will attach to ticket.
sasha: Will open a follow-up infra task to add a safety check: if token scope is exclusive to dedicated pools and we only have hosted fallback available, return 503 with clear error and avoid billing-hosted. That reduces auth confusion and billing surprises.
maria: Customer wants ETA. Can we give immediate remediation steps? leo?
leo: Short-term ETA: we can pause the drain (if patch isn't critical) in ~15m and migrate ACME to dedicated-eu-2 within 45m. Billing ops notified. Medium-term patch for token-rewrite/fallback is a 2-week effort.
support-bot: Ticket #TKT-4583 updated: pending infra rollback and billing review. Assigned to leo, aj, sasha.
aj: I'll attach the repro script and a filtered routing log and ping billing. maria, pls update the customer with the rollback window and that we're covering hosted cost for the spike.
maria: Doing that now. Leaving notes in the ticket: cause=drain-triggered-spillover + auth-scope-mismatch -> 401s -> hosted-billing. Repro steps included. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: drain canceled for dedicated-eu-1 by leo at 11:28:05 UTC. Current capacity restored to 100%.
sasha: Once stable, I'll schedule the token fallback design review with auth team. :calendar:
leo: Closing loop: monitor routing for acme-inc for next 6h; if any hosted routing shows up, auto-escalate.
maria: Thanks team — I'll send the customer a summary and the billing promise."
